standard.title: Health and social outcomes
standard.description: participate in physical activities that promote health and social outcomes to design and evaluate participation strategies for themselves and others
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can design, apply and evaluate personalised strategies for incorporating physical activity into their lives (AC9HP10M04). At Y9-10 this standard shifts focus from individual fitness planning to the social dimensions of physical activity participation — designing strategies that promote both health and social connection for themselves and others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in physical activities that promote health and social outcomes, and design and evaluate participation strategies for themselves and others.

nodes.label: Physical activity for social outcomes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and participate in physical activities that promote social outcomes alongside health benefits
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one physical activity with a clear social dimension; identify one health and one social outcome it promotes
nodes.typical_width: Participate in physical activities that promote health and social outcomes; identify local natural resources and community spaces where individuals and groups can connect through physical and social activities; investigate community-based campaigns promoting physical activity participation
wider: Investigate how culturally significant physical activities create community connection and belonging — evaluate the social outcomes these activities produce beyond physical health benefits
Identify and visit or research local natural settings for physical activity in the community — evaluate how accessible they are for different groups and what could increase their use
Participate in or investigate a community campaign promoting physical activity — determine the key elements that made it successful and evaluate whether they could be replicated in a school context

response_modes.reason: Social outcomes from physical activity are highly context-dependent — what builds community connection in one cultural or community setting differs from another. Students need to engage with multiple activity types and community contexts to develop genuine understanding of how physical activity produces social outcomes, not just health ones.

success_criteria: Names a specific physical activity and identifies both a health and a social outcome it promotes
Distinguishes social outcomes (e.g. connection, belonging, inclusion) from health outcomes (e.g. fitness, wellbeing)
Identifies at least one community space or resource where the activity could be pursued

nodes.label: Designing participation strategies for others
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design and evaluate participation strategies for physical activities that promote health and social outcomes for themselves and others
nodes.minimum_width: Design one strategy for increasing participation in a physical activity with health and social benefits; explain who it is designed for and why it would be effective for that group
nodes.typical_width: Create and evaluate proposals to promote use of natural settings for physical activity; design strategies involving family, friends and community in culturally significant physical activities that promote connection and belonging; evaluate participation strategies against health and social outcome goals
wider: Design and evaluate a strategy to involve a specific community group (e.g. elderly residents, culturally and linguistically diverse community members) in a physical activity that promotes health and social connection — justify design choices for that specific group
Create a proposal for a community celebration based around culturally significant physical activities — evaluate how it would promote a sense of belonging for diverse community members
Investigate and evaluate a school-based physical activity participation strategy — identify what elements are working, what barriers exist, and propose specific improvements based on evidence

response_modes.reason: Students commonly design participation strategies without evaluating whether they will work for the intended audience — designing a strategy for 'everyone' without considering what barriers different groups face. The structured reasoning investment is in making the design decisions explicit: who is this for, what barriers do they face, how does this strategy address those barriers, how will health and social outcomes be achieved.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Designing for a specific marginalised or culturally distinct group, culturally significant celebration design, and school-based strategy evaluation each require applying design and evaluation capability to a specific community context with distinct needs. Students who engage the wider tier develop the ability to design participation strategies that are genuinely inclusive rather than generically 'for everyone'.
success_criteria: Designs a strategy for a named target group — not a generic strategy
Strategy promotes both health and social outcomes — addresses both, not only one
Evaluation addresses whether the strategy is realistic and accessible for the target group
